steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Define an evidence-gated agency contract for AI tasks, action rights, human handoffs, interruption, fallback, and graduated autonomy.
hard_gates: No action right expands without task-specific evidence, a named human owner, observable bounds, interruption, rollback or containment, and explicit approval.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: A task definition, agent capabilities, human roles, failure cost, and observed behavior.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Classify an approved AI opportunity and route its model/data, agency, interaction, and safety questions to atomic specialist contracts without solving them here.
hard_gates: Routing cannot pass by renaming one giant AI design: every unresolved model/data, agency, interaction, authorization, and safety question must remain assigned to its specialist owner.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: A customer problem, AI opportunity thesis, quality target, cost constraint, and capability-selection question.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Design a bounded model, prompt, retrieval, data-rights, freshness, routing, cost, and evaluation architecture for an approved AI capability.
hard_gates: No model or data path may be recommended without lawful authority, provenance, minimization, freshness and deletion behavior, evaluation slices, failure fallback, and migration or rollback.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: An AI task, data sources, latency and cost constraints, model options, and quality targets.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Present already-developed architecture candidates as traceable comparable views, rankings, diagrams, and a bounded recommendation without inventing options or implementing one.
hard_gates: Candidates may be ranked only against the same declared criteria and evidence basis; missing evidence, human preference, and uncertainty cannot be converted into fabricated scores.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: Already discovered architecture candidates with code evidence.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Design one module boundary and interface that hides complexity, enforces dependency direction, preserves seams, and supports migration and verification.
hard_gates: A module is not deeper merely because code moved: the proposed interface must hide material complexity, reduce caller knowledge, preserve behavior, and have an incremental migration and rollback path.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: A module, its interfaces and dependencies, or evidenced architectural friction.
outputs: compatibility, migration, rollback, and test plan

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Find evidence-backed shallow modules, leaked boundaries, repeated orchestration, and change hotspots, and recommend deepen or leave unchanged under YAGNI.
hard_gates: No deepening candidate passes on aesthetics or hypothetical reuse alone; it needs cited recurring friction, boundary leakage, change coupling, or operational cost that exceeds migration risk.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: A codebase, change hotspots, repeated logic, and maintenance-friction evidence.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Generate at least two independent interface alternatives and compare information hiding, caller complexity, dependencies, failure behavior, testability, compatibility, and migration cost.
hard_gates: Alternatives must differ in responsibility boundary or information hiding; cosmetic signature variants do not satisfy divergent architecture evaluation.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: A bounded module problem, constraints, and an interface-design objective.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Define and verify subject, resource, action, context, tenancy, privileged-path, service-identity, audit, and default-deny authorization contracts.
hard_gates: Authentication is not authorization: any missing or untrusted subject, resource, action, context, tenancy, ownership, or policy version must fail closed at a server-side enforcement point.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: Actors, resources, operations, trust boundaries, tenancy model, authentication context, and risk policy.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Audit and minimally harden authorized CI workflow source for least privilege, immutable pinning, untrusted input, secret isolation, provenance, and safe rollback.
hard_gates: Untrusted pull-request code, metadata, artifacts, caches, or user-controlled strings must never execute in a context with secrets, write tokens, deployment identity, or unquoted command construction.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: CI workflow files, repository policy, trust boundaries, permissions, and runner context.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Define versioned data schemas, invariants, migration and rollback, API shapes, validation, errors, pagination, idempotency, concurrency, compatibility, and authorization hooks before implementation.
hard_gates: No contract passes without explicit compatibility, idempotency or retry behavior, concurrency semantics, validation and error shapes, authorization hooks, and a verified migration path with rollback or declared point of no return.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: Approved requirements, domain entities, existing persistence and interfaces, consistency needs, and compatibility constraints.
outputs: versioned data schema and invariant contract
migration, backfill, verification, and rollback plan
compatibility, idempotency, concurrency, and test matrix

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Independently review an implementation plan for architecture, interfaces, data, failure modes, security, operability, migration, verification, and execution risk without editing it.
hard_gates: A plan cannot pass on completeness of prose: every material architecture, data, security, migration, failure, and verification claim must trace to approved intent and an executable evidence path.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: Approved requirements, plan, architecture context, constraints, and existing system evidence.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Audit and minimally repair authorized frontend source so server-only logic, credentials, privileged actions, assets, dependencies, and runtime assumptions remain on safe explicit boundaries.
hard_gates: No server credential, secret-derived value, privileged authorization decision, filesystem or process API, or unsafe dynamic dependency may cross into a client bundle or browser-executable path.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: A frontend implementation, dependency graph, rendering environment, and integration constraints.
outputs: minimal authorized source or dependency patch

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Define secret classes, owners, environment boundaries, injection, least exposure, logging and redaction, rotation, revocation, retention, and incident procedures without accessing values.
hard_gates: Secret values must never be requested, read, printed, copied, transformed, hashed into evidence, persisted, or sent to a model; verification uses names, references, metadata, policy, and behavior only.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: Secret classes, environments, providers, CI/runtime paths, owners, rotation requirements, and authorization.

steps.condition: Select only when the atomic requested outcome matches: Independently threat-model and audit supplied architecture, source, dependencies, infrastructure, CI, secrets metadata, AI, and skill supply chain using authorized local checks, without remediation.
hard_gates: A security finding requires a cited trust boundary, reproducible evidence, exploit preconditions, impact, and severity rationale; audit permission never implies destructive testing, source repair, credential access, or remote mutation.
Review, reporting, contract, and audit candidates never imply implementation, live policy change, production mutation, or risk acceptance.
inputs: Architecture, code, dependencies, infrastructure evidence, trust boundaries, and test authorization.
